meta.title: Loose change on the floor of a mall in a day

prompt: How much change (in rupees) would you find on the floor of an average mall in a day?

clarifications.answer: Assume only coins are dropped, not notes; the mall is open 16 hours a day.
Two floors of ~300,000 usable sq ft each (600,000 total); an average store is 100 x 100 = 10,000 sq ft, so about 60 stores.
Split the day into high rush (4 h, 1500/h), medium rush (6 h, 1000/h) and low rush (6 h, 500/h).
Assume 50% of customers pay by cash, 5% of cash payers drop a coin, and an average dropped coin is worth Rs 2.

common_traps: Estimating footfall at one flat rate instead of splitting the day into rush bands.
Forgetting the chain of fractions: cash payers, then coin-droppers, then coin value.
Sizing the mall by total area rather than usable area net of corridors and common space.

anchors.1: Guesses a rupee figure with no footfall-times-loss-rate chain.
anchors.3: Estimates footfall but applies loss rates loosely or skips a step.
anchors.5: Builds daily footfall then applies cash-share, drop-rate and coin-value in sequence.

anchors.1: One flat footfall rate for the whole day.
anchors.3: Splits the day but with rush rates not clearly reasoned.
anchors.5: Splits the day into high/medium/low rush with distinct hourly rates.

anchors.1: Chains the fractions incorrectly; lands orders of magnitude off.
anchors.3: Reaches a number with a slip, landing just outside 400-1200.
anchors.5: Carries the footfall and fraction math cleanly, landing near 750 rupees.

anchors.3: Mentions a check but does not complete it.
anchors.5: Cross-checks that ~15000 visitors dropping the odd coin yields a small, believable few-hundred-rupee total.
